title: What if Chris Nolan were to adapt American Tabloid

commenti.body:
Please no. The book has a wildly complicated storyline which Nolan would use as a means to make the film ‘difficult’ and he doesn’t have the screenwriting chops to do justice to the dialogue. 

I know Curtis Hanson did a fantastic job on bringing LA confidential to the screen but as a massive American tabloid fan, I feel the book can only be tackled correctly by long form television. 

I am prepared for the downvotes.

I’m a fan of the entire Underworld series by Ellroy. Nolan is an interesting idea for a director if it were to be adapted, since it is certainly a challenge as noted.

There is an audio adaptation available on [Audible.com](https://www.audible.com/pd/B0CJ1BRJKD?source_code=ASSORAP0511160006&share_location=pdp). It features some big names like Brian Cox playing Howard Hughes.

I think my vote for who to direct a screen adaptation would be the Coen Brothers. And I’ve always viewed it as better suited for an episodic production instead of a feature.

No, you’re right. It’s too dense for a movie. The fact that LA Confidential turned out as well as it did was kind of a minor miracle. A series that covers the whole USA Underground trilogy with maybe a season or two seasons per book as needed would be ideal.
Fincher is locked in a deal with Netflix for now. Given how Mindhunter is going nowhere, maybe American Tabloid is a good deal. However, he would need a good screenwriter
I’d love Fincher to have a pop at it and agree the screen writer would be key. The book is so good I’d rather it not be made than made badly.

I second the Coen brothers or, of course, Tarantino. The entire underworld USA trilogy -but especially Bloods A Rover- is fun in a way that Tarantino is also fun. But it’s also so incredibly redemptive, and I think later era Tarantino would really capture that very well. Ellroy is very funny, and I don’t think Nolan really captures humor well. He’s not NOT funny, but he’s less humor forward than Ellroy’s writing. 

It’s my dream project to see at least one of those books brought to the big screen. Unfortunately due to the way The Cold Six Thousand both starts and ends I doubt it would ever happen.

What if? Well I know what night not to go to cinema! Nolan would create another male-centric film. And I’ve been really disappointed by Scorsese these past few films. I think he’s lost his touch. The only Nolan film I could stomach was Interstellar. Otherwise his style is just not my cup of tea. Scorsese had a great run all the way to 1995, but since then only Wolf of Wall Street has really shined. 

For the concept you’re describing, I’d like to see what a Clint Eastwood might come up with. He’s not always perfect. But when he gets it right, he knocks it out of the park. And can still do it now. Once he started his Unforgiven period, every few films he’s created stories that draw the viewer in. The Bridges of Madison County, Mystic River, Million Dollar Baby, Changeling, Gran Torino, American Sniper (sorry about the doll), and in 2019 Richard Jewell which I loved because it’s an exciting dramatic story, the lead actor is so good, and so is Kathy Bates. Yes Eastwood can slip up. But he can still bring it when he gets it right. And I highly recommend Unforgiven, I got to see it at the drive-thru movie theater at ten years old, and it’s considered the best Eastwood film. 

Back to Scorsese, he’s also going to put Leonardo in it. I don’t know how they pulled off Wolf of Wall Street. That’s actually good. I first saw Leo on American sitcom Growing Pains. He was arguably (and please debate and discuss this) good in What’s Eating Gilbert Grape. Then he became a teen heartthrob, then a “serious actor.” Some people just insist upon themselves and wear out their welcome. Angelina Jolie and Alec Baldwin. One more reason I wouldn’t go to the film you’re describing.

Fincher and Ellroy are good friends, and Fincher was working on a series at HBO with Ellroy called Confidential that was going to be about Freddy Otash, but Fincher blew the budget up with his meticulous directing style. As I recall, the budget for the pilot ballooned passed the budget for later era GoT.

it wuz right there for Oliver Stone to hate-direct in the late 90s.

now the time has passed.

what if...J C Chandor had gone here after "A Violent Year" instead of the Faustian bargain of "Triple Frontier" with netflix...

Agree. Nolan is just too analytical and cerebral, and Ellroy is just so HOT and emotional. 

Nolan is perfect for lots of things, but American Tabloid isnt it.
Why would Oliver Stone make two JFK Assassination movies?

I know Nolan sounds like an odd choice for adapting Ellroy's work. But, he has proven that he can handle adaptations, like Memento, Insomnia, The Prestige, and more recently, Oppenheimer. I agree, Oppenheimer was stuffed with too much info, but the pacing was racy enough, the exposition was tight, and almost everyone had at least one memorable scene. For some reason, I see Oppenheimer as Nolan's attempt to craft a 3-dimensional protagonist.   


In the case of American Tabloid, he already has the story. So, he can't mess up with the characters or the narrative. He has a reliable cast to deliver the performance.  


And if he is never to be considered, well, there's always the Coen Brothers, as someone else has pointed out already. I would've said Tarantino only if he hadn't announced his final project.
So, what other work would you like to see Nolan adapt? I'm curious
